hook.text: One lump of flesh. A hundred sons.

boon.text: Gandhari cared for a weary sage, who granted her one hundred sons.

carry.text: She carried the child two years.

kunti.text: News came: her sister-in-law Kunti had a son, bright as the morning sun.
Then her sister-in-law bore a son, bright as the morning sun.

forced.text: In grief, without telling her husband, she forced the birth.

mass.text: Out came a mass of flesh, hard as iron.

vyasa.text: That sage, Vyasa, came: Fill a hundred pots with ghee. Sprinkle it with cold water.

split.text: It split into a hundred and one parts, each the size of a thumb joint.

pots.text: Each went into its pot, under guard. Duryodhana was born first.
Each went into its pot. Duryodhana was born first.

omens.text: Jackals howled. The brahmins said: give this one up.

refuse.text: For love of his son, the king would not.

daughter.text: Within a month all hundred were born, then one daughter: Duhshala.
